checks.primaryClaim: ED record: 20-25 working days end-to-end ('The end-to-end process, from plan approval through license registration to certificate download, takes approximately 20 to 25 working days'), with the basis described as 'UT-level administrative practice, not a statutory turnaround prescribed under the Factories Act, 1948'. FGD record: inspection-mandated (Orange/Red) categories take 'up to around 25 days'.
checks.sourceSays: The notified UT (Right of Citizens to Public Services) Rules, 2022, Schedule-I, Sr. No. 27 (Department: 'Factories and Boilers') lists '1 | Registration of license under The Factories Act, 1948 | 20' days, '2 | Renewal of license under The Factories Act, 1948 | 10' and '3 | Approval of plan and permission to construct/extend/or take into use any building as a factory under the Factories Act, 1948 | 15'. Rule 6 of the same Rules provides: 'The public holidays shall not be included while calculating the stipulated time limit for delivery of service and the number of days where the applicant has not responded to any query of the department shall not be included in calculation of time limit.' The same 20-day figure is published on the UT's EODB Single Window Portal Factories & Boilers department page ('Registration of license under The Factories Act, 1948 | Factories & Boiler | 20 Days' under the column heading 'Timeline (Working Days)') and in the department's own service checklist ('5 Timelines 20 days').

checks.sourceSays: An order of the UT Administration's own Department of Labour & Employment states: 'Therefore, the Single Window / Online System set up by the UT Administration of Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu shall accord deemed approvals / clearances / recommendation (as the case may be), in case the concerned approving department / authority does not provide clearances within their specified timelines as per "Samay Sudhini Seva" or prescribed time lines under applicable Laws / Regulations / Rules in respect of the following Services'. Under the heading 'Department of Factories & Boilers:-' the table lists 'Reform No. 103 | Registration of Factories under the Factories Act, 1948 / Factory Licence | 20 Days (Working Days) | Chief Inspector of Factories & Boiler'. It continues: 'Aforesaid Services are to be provided in prescribed time limit, failing which approval would be granted by Single Window / Online System to the applicant and Responsibility of the Officer/ Official shall be fixed for causing delay in providing services in time bound manner & necessary departmental proceeding may be initiated against the concern.' and 'Further if any query / clarification related to investor's application, the concern department will communicate the same to the applicant once and within 7 days of receipt of the application.' Separately, the DRAFT DNH & DD Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Rules, 2026 (not yet finalised) would put the deemed-grant period at thirty days: rule 96(3) 'The license under this rule shall be issued within thirty days from the date of application on portal complete in all respect' and rule 96(4) 'If the designated authority fails to grant license to a factory ... within the period of thirty days, then such license shall deemed to have been granted on the expiration of thirty days' (also rule 149(4): 'If the authority fails to grant or reject such application within the prescribed time, the license shall be deemed to be issued and auto generated').

remarks: MOST SIGNIFICANT FINDING — the ED-vs-FGD deemed-approval contradiction is resolved in favour of the FGD participants. An order of the UT's own Department of Labour & Employment (No. LE/LI/DMN/BRAP/SW/2020/340 dated 6-9-2020, signed by the Secretary (Labour), DNH & DD) directs that the Single Window / Online System 'shall accord deemed approvals / clearances / recommendation' where the department does not deliver within the specified timeline, and expressly names 'Registration of Factories under the Factories Act, 1948 / Factory Licence — 20 Days (Working Days)' in its Factories & Boilers table. A deemed-approval mechanism for the Factory Licence therefore exists in writing and is published on the UT's own EODB portal, contrary to the ED expert's statement that there is none. The FGD participants' 25-day figure is not the notified number: the order fixes 20 working days. Note this is an administrative order, not a gazette notification; the underlying UT (Right of Citizens to Public Services) Rules, 2022 notify the same 20-day service limit but themselves contain no deemed-approval clause (only auto-escalation of grievances and appeals).

Three different deemed/limit periods are now on the record and should not be conflated: 20 working days (in force today, per the 2020 Labour Department order and the notified RTS Rules, 2022 Schedule-I); 25 days (FGD participants' recollection, not matched by any source found); and 30 days (DRAFT DNH & DD OSHWC Rules, 2026, rule 96(3)-(4) and rule 149(4), which would supersede the present regime once finalised).

DRAFT-STATUS WARNING: the DNH & DD Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Rules, 2026 (notification No. LE/LI/OSHWC/210539/2026/220 dated 20-07-2026, 271 pages) are expressly a draft published for objections, not finalised gazetted text. They are cited here only as supporting/secondary material inside the deemedApproval and fees checks, never as the sole basis of a verdict. As of this session the Labour & Employment document listing on ddd.gov.in still shows only the 20/07/2026 DRAFT versions of the OSHWC, Industrial Relations, Social Security and Wages rules — no finalised notification has been published there, so the Goa, Daman & Diu Factories Rules / DNH Factories Rules regime and its 2015/2016 fee schedule remain the operative text.

On fees, two different ceilings exist and the ED's 'approximately Rs. 1 lakh' matches the DRAFT, not the rules in force. The notified Schedule to rule 6(2) (Goa, Daman and Diu Factories (Amendment) Rules, 2015) tops out at Rs. 47,200 per year; the draft OSHWC Rules, 2026 Schedule-I ('Fees for the grant of license for a factory for one calendar year', load in kilowatts x number of workers) runs from Rs. 1,000 to Rs. 1,00,000. Both schedules are computed on connected power and worker count — corroborating the FGD's description of the portal's fee calculator — but neither uses the pollution category (Green/Orange/Red) that FGD participants also mentioned. The FGD's example of 'roughly Rs. 22,000' is consistent with the notified 2015 matrix, which contains a Rs. 22,400 cell. The 'lower tenure' option the ED mentions is real: licences/renewals may be taken for a period not exceeding 10 years at the annual rate multiplied by the number of years.

The ED record leaves portal.url null; the portal it names is live and was fetched this session at https://swp.dddgov.in/ (note: swp.dddgov.in, not swp.ddd.gov.in, which does not resolve). This also supersedes the source list's note that investdd.gov.in was unreachable — swp.dddgov.in is the working single-window instrument and hosts the Factory Licence service, its checklist, its timeline table and the deemed-approval order.

Nothing found this session adjudicates the ED-vs-FGD disagreement about site inspection (ED: a safety officer inspection is always required and there is no risk-based classification; FGD: no physical inspection for Green/self-declaration cases, only for Orange/Red). The official published procedure for the licence lists five online steps with no inspection step, and the draft OSHWC rule 96 likewise prescribes no pre-grant inspection, but absence from a procedure page is not an official statement that no inspection occurs — hence 'steps' is marked confirmed only as to the online single-window process, and the inspection question remains open.

Two listed services carry timelines that differ between official sources and should be flagged if the dashboard ever shows renewal: renewal of the factory licence is 10 days in the notified RTS Rules, 2022 Schedule-I but is displayed as '60 Days' on the EODB portal's Factories & Boilers page. The grant/registration figure (20 days) is consistent across all three official sources.

https://labourdnhdd.in/documents/notification-form/6348f7ddd67a6.pdf, linked from the EODB portal as the primary copy of the 10-year-validity reform notification, returned HTTP 404 this session; the same notification was read from the portal's own mirror (reform_109_v2.pdf, byte-identical to Reform_114_v1.pdf). https://swp.dddgov.in/assets/department/sss/reforms_2_Labour.pdf is byte-identical (md5 1a19a5473a1e43d5b42e7801b06fbeb9) to reform_103.pdf, i.e. the deemed-approval order is published twice on the portal, under both the Factories & Boilers reform list and the 'Time Bound Delivery of Services' page.

The two 2026 Right of Citizens to Public Services (Amendment) Rules notifications (draft, Extraordinary No. 44 of 30-06-2026, and final, Extraordinary No. 57 of 17-08-2026) were read and contain no service-wise timelines or deemed-approval provision for factory licensing; they only strengthen grievance redressal (auto-generated complaints and automatically escalated first appeals). They are listed under sourcesRead as fetched-but-not-dispositive.
